mbm-1476.clue: I play nine holes with a paper fish.
mbm-1476.quote: I folded a fish from an old scorecard and tucked it beneath the strap of my golf bag. Its little tail twitches before the grass shows a breeze. My regular playing partner asks the fish before he asks me.

mbm-1477.clue: I picked my landing by the laundry.
mbm-1477.quote: From the air the drop zone was a pale square beside a farmhouse. Somebody had hung one scarlet sheet on the line. I remember that splash of red more clearly than any arrow on the instructor’s map.

mbm-1478.clue: I wait for the second pair of hands.
mbm-1478.quote: At our son evenings the room always starts with one person clapping. I hold my claves until another rhythm joins it. That’s the moment the porch stops feeling like a porch and starts feeling like a band.

mbm-1479.clue: I put a pocket in the curtain.
mbm-1479.quote: I hemmed the café curtains and stitched a tiny pocket behind the last fold for a pencil. The owner uses it to take down customers’ requests. Most of the requests turn out to be pie.

mbm-1480.clue: I went back for a green coat.
mbm-1480.quote: I took my aunt back to the cinema to see the green coat in my favorite film. Before we even took our seats, a woman walked past in the very same coat. My aunt held up her red gloves. The woman had those too.

mbm-1481.clue: I signed the jump log with my thumb.
mbm-1481.quote: I’d forgotten my pen on the day of my first solo parachute landing. My instructor took an ink pad from the office and I pressed a thumbprint beside his neat signature. It looked like a very small landing field.

mbm-1482.clue: I gave the climbing hold a weather report.
mbm-1482.quote: The round blue hold at our wall always feels cold first thing in the morning. We call it the moon. I finally reached past it in the evening sun and my friend announced a very warm night in space.

mbm-1483.clue: I keep the last tally for my coach.
mbm-1483.quote: My coach kept a chalk tally on the board for each weight set I finished. I drew sunflower petals around the tallies at the end. We took a picture of the flower before the next class needed the space.

mbm-1484.clue: I can hear which neighbor just arrived.
mbm-1484.quote: At our domino table one friend knocks once on the wood and another slides his first tile in without a sound. I can deal a hand with my eyes closed and still know who needs the chair with the cushion.

mbm-1485.clue: I keep the green thread on a shell.
mbm-1485.quote: My aunt wraps her embroidery floss around little smooth shells. She lent me a green one for the leaves on a pollera panel. I returned it with one tiny stitched leaf tied to the end.

mbm-1486.clue: I mixed that green with a train ticket.
mbm-1486.quote: I had forgotten my palette knife, so I stirred two colors with the corner of an old ticket. The wet corner printed a perfect little hillside on the back of my hand. I matched my whole landscape to that green.

mbm-1487.quote: At anime club I sketch the things a character leaves on the table after they walk away. My favorite episode ends with a teacup still steaming. I pinned my sketch beside the real kettle.

mbm-1488.clue: I made the batting from an old blanket.
mbm-1488.quote: Dad’s plaid blanket had worn thin enough to see through. I slipped it between new quilt layers for him. We stood by the window and lifted one corner for a last look at the old plaid before I stitched it shut.

mbm-1489.clue: I make station portraits from the benches.
mbm-1489.quote: I take the same seat at different stops and draw the view over the empty track. My book flips from a brick chimney to a river to three greenhouses. It’s a train journey you can take with your thumb.

mbm-1490.clue: I cut the blue pieces twice.
mbm-1490.quote: I cut a quilt block to match the blue of Mum’s bicycle. Then she repainted it. I stitched the new shade beside the old and made the block a pair of wheels turning together.

mbm-1491.clue: I keep a length of yellow string on my paddle bag.
mbm-1491.quote: We ran a tiny string between our canoe and a floating pinecone to show my nephew how a tow works. The pinecone steered itself around every twig. My nephew promoted it to captain before we reached the bank.

mbm-1492.clue: I fold the courtyard into the paper.
mbm-1492.quote: I made a papel picado banner of cut-out balconies. When we hung it across the courtyard, their shadows fell right under the real balconies. Our aunt opened her shutters and waved from both levels.

mbm-1493.clue: I lost count at the third apple.
mbm-1493.quote: I juggle wooden apples painted in shades of ripeness. My niece says the red one must land in the basket first. She makes the rules up, but she’s made my aim much better.

mbm-1494.clue: I’ve quilted a whole set of chipped cups.
mbm-1494.quote: Our cupboard holds a cup for every aunt and uncle, each with its own familiar nick. I pieced the cups across a quilt and gave every one its chip. Nobody has to look at a name to find their place.

mbm-1495.clue: I take the little broom camping.
mbm-1495.quote: After pitching the tent I sweep the doorstep with a broom just longer than my hand. My friends teased me until pine needles filled their sleeping bags. The broom now travels in the best side pocket.

mbm-1496.clue: I follow the paper map’s fold.
mbm-1496.quote: My canoe route happens to trace a creek straight along a crease in the map. I drew a little blue arrow across the fold. Open the paper and the water seems to pour right onto the table.

mbm-1497.clue: I always rescue the clock before the rain.
mbm-1497.quote: When a shower hits our park chess table my partner scoops up the pieces and I shelter the clock. We set everything back up under the bandstand and continue to the sound of water drumming overhead.

mbm-1498.clue: I kept one star from the disco ball.
mbm-1498.quote: A little mirror tile came loose during cleanup at the club. The owner let me glue it to my record box. When I open the lid a tiny patch of light skips across the wall ahead of the music.

mbm-1499.clue: I painted the fan from the middle out.
mbm-1499.quote: I put a little orange fox across the folds so its tail appears last when I open the fan. My cousin likes to open it just halfway and challenge people to guess who is hiding behind the tree.

mbm-1500.clue: I keep a sketch of the museum bench.
mbm-1500.quote: I spent an hour drawing the long blue bench opposite my favorite painting because that’s where my parents used to sit together. The curator saw the sketch and told me the carpenter’s name. I wrote it beneath the bench.
